access.edition_or_version: Essays in Idleness: The Tsurezuregusa of Kenko, trans. Donald Keene (Columbia University Press, 1967)

mechanics.premise: Miscellaneous reflections on impermanence, taste and conduct, gathered without a single thesis.
mechanics.argumentative_stance: Observational and generalising: a particular custom or scene becomes a claim about how to live with transience.
mechanics.point_of_view: Essayistic observer moving between personal memory and general statement.
mechanics.structure: Zuihitsu ('follow-the-brush') sequence of short independent sections unified only by recurring preoccupations.
mechanics.style_and_devices: Aphoristic observation, contrast between the fashionable and the enduring, understatement.
mechanics.imagery: Seasonal and architectural images (blossoms, ruins, moonlight) carrying abstract claims about impermanence.
mechanics.emotional_progression: Wistful attention resolving into calm acceptance.
mechanics.critical_reception: A classic of Japanese literature and a standard example of the zuihitsu form.
mechanics.failure_or_misuse_signals: Picturesque observation without generalisation becomes tone-reflective or nostalgic, not philosophical.
